item.title: Optimization of Urban Shortest Path Considering Traffic Congestion and Air Quality Using ICAW and Genetic Algorithm (Case Study: Tehran)
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — This study proposes a multi-objective framework for optimizing urban shortest paths by simultaneously considering traffic congestion and air quality. The objective is to minimize a weighted combination of travel time and pollutant exposure, with binary decision variables representing route selection. Real-world air quality data (SO₂, NO₂, CO) were collected from IoT sensors on 500 vehicles and 50 fixed stations across Tehran, integrated with traffic data via spatio-temporal synchronization using inverse distance weighting and 500m grid mapping. item.title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a disaster-aware privacy-preserving federated learning (PP-FL) solution for multi-city traffic flow prediction in heterogeneous and non-IID data settings. item.title: Bridging the Educational Gap with Virtual Reality (VR): Virtual Labs for the Next Generation
item.description: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science — This research addresses the systemic educational inequality in Thailand, where a severe shortage of physical science laboratories in rural areas hinders the development of 21st-century scientific literacy. Using the ADDIE model, the study developed a virtual world technology innovation, the AR SciLab platform, to serve as a high-quality, risk-free learning infrastructure. The innovation comprises a database of eight career-oriented experiments (e.g., biodiesel production and essential oil extraction), 3D immersive VR environments built on Unreal Engine 5, and bilingual instructional media. item.description: PhilPapers (PhilPapers Foundation) — Segregation research increasingly measures who people encounter beyond home, yet physical mobility, place semantics, and digital activity are often combined without clear construct boundaries. This study develops a physical--digital activity-space framework that distinguishes co-presence, digital exposure, and digital interaction, and represents physical and digital segregation as separate components rather than a forced composite. item.title: SUSTAINABLE MOBILITY AND TERRITORIAL ACCESSIBILITY IN MANIZALES, COLOMBIA: SOCIAL COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS OF AN EXPANDED AERIAL CABLE NETWORK
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — This research evaluates the socioeconomic feasibility of expanding the aerial cable car system in Manizales and Villamaría, Colombia, through a Social Cost-Benefit Analysis (SCBA). The assessment compares the three operational lines with a projected nine-line network, based on the Manizales Land Use Plan. The objective is to quantify and monetize impacts on CO2eq emissions, territorial accessibility, road safety, and public health benefits derived from induced active mobility. item.title: The Geography of Euroleague Basketball: Spatial Inequality, Travel Exposure and Home-Court Advantage in a Transnational League
item.description: Geosport for Society — This study conceptualizes the EuroLeague as a transnational urban network and tests whether spatial position and nominal travel distance are associated with competitive outcomes. The design integrates three empirical layers: (i) a longitudinal spatial panel covering the league-format era from 2016-17 to 2025-26; (ii) a completed 2025- 26 cross-section of 20 clubs in 17 nominal urban nodes and 11 countries; and (iii) a game-level model based on 1,943 available regular-season games from seven analytically retained seasons between 2016-17 and 2024-25. item.title: STRATEGIC SPATIAL PLANNING FOR ENHANCING THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF THE TOURISM SECTOR IN GOA, INDIA
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. The analysis uses a 1 × 1 km grid across Goa and integrates tourism amenity indicators, environmental conditions, accessibility measures, and regulatory constraints. item.title: DELINEATION OF AGRICULTURAL FIELD BOUNDARIES USING MACHINE LEARNING: BASED ON THE CASE OF THE ZHETYSAI DISTRICT, KAZAKHSTAN
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is essential for agro-production monitoring, irrigation management, and sustainable land use planning. Manual digitization is labour-intensive and poorly scalable, while conventional segmentation algorithms are sensitive to spectral heterogeneity and weak inter-field contrast. The Zhetysai district of southern Kazakhstan – where approximately 45-50% of irrigated farmland exhibits salinization – exemplifies the urgent demand for automated field mapping. item.title: MORE MONUMENTS, MORE TOURISTS? EXAMINING HERITAGE-TOURISM RELATIONSHIPS ACROSS ROMANIAN COUNTIES
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Cultural heritage is an important territorial resource for tourism development, yet the relationship between the distribution of listed heritage assets and tourism activity remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the geographical relationships between listed cultural heritage and tourism in Romania, focusing on territorial disparities and long-term changes. item.title: Rethinking Women’s Football Attendance in an Emerging Destination: Constraints, Marketing Awareness and Interest through a Pluriversal Lens
item.description: Geosport for Society — Women’s football is increasingly recognised as an important component of the sport tourism industry, with potential to diversify audiences, stimulate domestic travel, and advance gender inclusivity in emerging destinations. Yet, despite the growing interest, attendance remains inconsistent, complicating conventional measures of spectator demand. item.description: Revista de Aplicaciones de la Ingeniería — In this article we highlight the importance of monitoring polluting particles in cities. This is to contribute to achieving sustainability objectives. Air pollution by suspended particles, especially PM2.5 and PM10, is a serious public health problem in urban areas of Mexico, with measurable impacts on respiratory and cardiovascular mortality and morbidity. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Illegal trade in lobster pueruli (Benih Bening Lobster, BBL) presents interconnected challenges for fisheries governance, coastal livelihoods, and Indonesia’s maritime defense. This study examines how changes in BBL utilization policies, legal market access, and commodity traceability create potential vulnerabilities that may be exploited by smuggling networks. item.title: From Maritime Picture to Customs Risk Picture: Strengthening Indonesian Customs through Maritime Domain Awareness
item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Indonesia’s customs administration operates at the intersection of maritime mobility, trade facilitation, border protection, and revenue assurance, yet its risk systems are still primarily organized around declarations, manifests, entities, and transactions rather than the wider maritime operating picture. This article develops a conceptual model for transforming Maritime Domain Awareness into a Customs Risk Picture that can support earlier, more contextual, and more explainable targeting of vessels, voyages, cargoes, and commercial actors. item.title: Between emergency and reconstruction: Territorial impacts and climate adaptation challenges after hurricane John in Guerrero
item.description: ECORFAN eBooks — This chapter analyses the territorial, human, and socioeconomic impacts caused by Hurricane John (2024) in the state of Guerrero, with a particular focus on the municipalities of Acapulco and Coyuca de Benítez, within a context of increasing intensity and frequency of extreme hydrometeorological events. item.title: PROTECTION OF FAMILIES AFFECTED BY THE MOUNT SEMERU ERUPTION: A DISASTER FIQH PERSPECTIVE ON THE MDMC LUMAJANG RESPONSE
item.description: Jurnal Al-Ijtimaiyyah — The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru not only destroyed homes but also severed the social and economic networks of thousands of families in Lumajang Regency, demanding a disaster response grounded in Islamic normative principles alongside technical capacity. Muhammadiyah, through the Himpunan Putusan Tarjih (HPT), has formulated Disaster Fiqh as an ethical framework to safeguard the rights of disaster victims, yet studies examining how far humanitarian organizations’ field practices align with this framework at the family level remain scarce. item.description: Journal Labor and Demographic economics — This article examines the relationship between ancestral knowledge, artisanal production, and socioeconomic benefits in Tabasco through an integrative review of academic literature and official documents. The corpus covers embroidered strips, plant fibers, wood carving, drum making, and workshop organization, together with cultural statistics, legislation, and public programs. item.description: AIS Electronic Library (AISeL) — Digital content platforms must recommend new content before knowing its quality or audience fit, while early feedback is selectively shaped by prior allocation rules. Although exploration may support learning, direct evidence is limited regarding whether early random exploration improves the subsequent organic recommendation performance of new content by generating more informative feedback. item.title: Contribution of agricultural cooperatives and humanitarian assistance on food security resilience and rural development in Mali
item.description: ORBi (University of Liège) — Mali, located in the Sahel region, experiences a persistent food security crisis driven by climate variability, recurrent conflict, displacement, market disruptions, and structural weaknesses in rural systems. The agricultural sector, which supports the majority of households, is highly vulnerable to droughts, erratic rainfall, flooding, and insecurity. These factors undermine agricultural production, food access, and community resilience. item.title: Comparative Framework of Vulnerability in Coastal Communities of the Ecuadorian Tropics
item.description: Applied Planetary Health — This study conducts a comparative analysis of socio-ecological vulnerability in six coastal communities of the Ecuadorian tropics, integrating mixed methods (quantitative and qualitative). The conceptual framework based on the components of Exposure, Sensitivity, and Adaptive Capacity allowed the construction of a Comparative Coastal Vulnerability Index (CCVI). item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary intellectual and social movement that connects gender equality, environmental sustainability and social justice. It examines how systems of patriarchy, economic exploitation, unequal resource distribution and environmental degradation can reinforce one another. Emerging prominently during the 1970s and 1980s, eco-feminism has developed from an early emphasis on the symbolic relationship between women and nature toward broader approaches involving environmental justice, political ecology, intersectionality and sustainable development. item.description: Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University) — This research explored how access to everyday destinations influences neighborhood and social satisfaction among individuals with disabilities. It examined how factors such as sociodemographic characteristics, accessibility, and frequency of visits to places contribute to how people experience their neighborhoods and social lives. item.description: AHFE international — The presented study investigates associations between events influencing public transportation experience in both urban (Hamburg) and rural (Tuttlingen) areas in Germany, with the aim of identifying events associated with travel experience, which may in turn influence travel behavior. Using a mobile application, 21 participants in Tuttlingen and 70 participants in Hamburg tracked everyday trips, providing real-time evaluations of travel experiences along with situational data. item.title: Associations of redox conditions and organic matter with nickel and chromium partitioning in the Bahodopi River, a tropical lateritic mining river in Central Sulawesi
item.description: Journal of Ecological Engineering — Lateritic nickel mining can increase the transport of metal-bearing particles into river systems, where sediment–water partitioning governs metal mobility and ecological exposure. Although redox conditions and organic matter are recognized as factors associated with metal partitioning, their relative importance under tropical lateritic mining conditions remains poorly understood. item.description: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University) — Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disproportionately affects African American women and contributes to racial health disparities in the United States. Although genetic susceptibility influences disease risk, growing evidence suggests that social determinants of health (SDOH), including neighborhood conditions, structural racism, and socioeconomic disadvantage, contribute to disease development and progression. item.title: Decolonizing ecocriticism: Climate justice, Indigenous knowledge, and more-than-human agency in contemporary Anglophone literature
item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Contemporary climate fiction increasingly challenges the assumption that ecological crisis can be understood exclusively through universalized narratives of environmental degradation. Such narratives often obscure the historical inequalities through which ecological harm is produced and unevenly distributed. This article proposes a decolonizing approach to ecocriticism through a comparative reading of Imbolo Mbue’s How Beautiful We Were (2021) and Amitav Ghosh’s Gun Island (2019). item.description: CAUCHY Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi — Infrastructure development is important for reducing regional disparities, but Indonesian provinces differ in economic conditions, human resources, and regional characteristics. This study examines the relationships between the Economy, Human Resources, and Regional Characteristics and Infrastructure in the 38 provinces of Indonesia, based on secondary data from Statistics Indonesia (BPS) for 2024 and 2025. item.description: Frontiers in Sustainability — Cities need spatially explicit canopy information to connect urban greening with surface-temperature context, mobility, and neighborhood planning. item.title: Flexible but not free: The gendered flexibility paradox in Indonesia's gig economy
item.description: SIMULACRA JURNAL SOSIOLOGI — Female gig workers in Indonesia face challenges underexamined in a gig economy literature centered largely on Western contexts. Domestic scholarship has tended to treat gender as a descriptive variable within male-dominated sectors. This study examines how platform algorithms, gender norms, and household responsibilities shape women’s gig work across sectors. item.description: Frontiers in Sociology — Introduction Recurrent fires in South Africa's informal settlements are governed as technical emergencies, despite being produced and experienced through unequal infrastructures, insecure tenure, and uneven state protection. This study examines how young and older residents of fire-prone informal settlements in the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality interpret risk, respond to emergencies, negotiate recovery, and convert disaster experience into civic action. item.description: Population and Environment — Ambient air pollution is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes including stillbirth, miscarriage, and preterm birth. However, its effects on the viability, implantation, and survival of conceptuses – largely unobserved before the clinical detection of pregnancy – remain poorly understood. item.description: MARGIN ECO — Hydrometeorological disasters cause not only physical damage but also substantial disruptions to livelihoods and local economic activities. This study examines the economic impacts of hydrometeorological disasters and identifies priority strategies for post-disaster economic recovery in West Sumatra, Indonesia. item.description: Preprint / source unavailable — Introduction: Community and public health systems face persistent fragmentation, inequitable access, and limited capacity to respond to evolving population health needs. These challenges are intensified by epidemiological transitions, social inequalities, and uneven access to preventive and primary healthcare. item.description: Preprint / source unavailable — This study examines the gendered impacts of rice crop loss in Odisha, India, drawing on evidence from 409 farming households across eight rice-producing districts. Using household surveys, focus group discussions, and key informant interviews, the research explores how crop loss affects livelihoods, food security, health, education, migration, and household wellbeing. item.description: SIMULACRA JURNAL SOSIOLOGI — Makassar’s waste-to-energy (WtE) transition is promoted as a technological response to urban waste and clean-energy challenges, yet its social consequences remain insufficiently examined. This study investigates how planned WtE development restructures power relations, access to waste resources, and livelihood security among waste-dependent communities around the Tamangapa disposal site. item.description: Journal of economics, business and commerce. — The impact of trading place allocation on the performance of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Kamwala, Lusaka, is not well documented, even though allocation determines where each enterprise is located in the market. The study evaluated the influence of accessibility on sales performance, the role of strategic positioning in customer attraction, and the impact of trading place infrastructure on business development. item.description: Urbanization, sustainability and society. — Purpose Connection and proximity to nature are associated with improved wellbeing outcomes. Yet links between gentrification and urban greening mean socio-economic factors may override the predictive capacity of nearby nature on wellbeing. This study aims to explore relationships between connection with nature, socio-economic factors and attributes of nearby nature. item.description: Urban Forum — Across South Africa, local municipalities responsible for basic service delivery face growing financial, technical, infrastructural, and institutional strain. In many towns and rural municipalities, waste collection has become intermittent, uneven, and uncertain. Yet waste does not disappear when municipal systems weaken. item.title: Water stress as a pathway between climate vulnerability and fiscal sustainability in the European Union
item.description: Discover Environment — Climate vulnerability can affect fiscal sustainability through both direct effects and environmental pressures. This study examines whether water stress provides a pathway linking climate vulnerability to fiscal sustainability in the EU-27 over 2003–2023. item.title: Impact of Connected Vehicles on Transport Network Resilience Under Traffic Signal Attacks
item.description: Lecture notes in mobility — Cyberattacks on traffic signal systems pose growing risks to transport network resilience. Connected vehicles (CVs), through real-time communication and dynamic rerouting, may help mitigate these impacts, but their role under traffic signal attacks remains unclear. This paper investigates how transport network resilience changes under clustered and dispersed traffic signal attacks with different CV penetration rates. item.title: Inaccessible: Weakened Social Capital and Barriers to Getting by in a New Mexico Community During the COVID ‐19 Pandemic
item.description: Rural Sociology — This qualitative, county‐level study of 58 residents of a Hispanic‐majority community in northern New Mexico (summer 2021) reveals limitations to social capital during disasters or periods of prolonged strain. While previous research demonstrates that social capital sometimes bridges gaps in access for rural residents during ordinary times, this study shows that when the social and physical field shifts—as they did during the COVID‐19 pandemic—social capital is weakened and unable to fully provide the support that policy frameworks often anticipate. item.title: Dynamic Relationships Among Energy, Air Transport, ICT , and Economic Growth: Evidence From Emerging Economies
item.description: Sustainable Development — This study examines the associations of energy use, air transport activity and information and communication technology (ICT) with gross domestic product (GDP) per capita in 14 emerging economies during 1990–2023, and whether these infrastructures complement one another. After testing cross‐sectional dependence, unit roots and cointegration, a panel autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model is estimated using pooled mean group (PMG) and mean group (MG) estimators. item.title: Protective accessibility for resilient urban mobility under recurrent air threats
item.description: Discover Cities — Recurrent air threats turn civilian protection into a continuing condition of urban mobility. This study applies GIS-based cumulative-opportunity analysis to define the Protective Shelter Accessibility Index (PSI), a spatial screening measure of the average number of designated shelters reachable from public transport stops through the pedestrian network within 2-, 5- and 15-minute planning horizons. item.title: Delineate anything flow: fast, country-level field boundary detection from any source
item.description: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation — Accurate satellite data-based field boundary delineation is essential for land management and agricultural statistics, but integrating tile-level predictions into continuous large-area vector products introduces topological errors and computational challenges. We present Delineate Anything Flow (DelAnyFlow), a framework for scalable field instance mapping that integrates the YOLOv11-based DelAny model with structured post-processing, cross-tile instance unification, vectorization, and topology-consistent simplification. item.title: From financial difficulty to financial resilience: the role of financial inclusion, gender, and geography in Saudi Arabia
item.description: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications — Financial resilience has become an increasingly important dimension of financial wellbeing, reflecting individuals’ capacity to cope with financial shocks and maintain economic stability over time. This study examines financial difficulty and financial resilience as interconnected positions along a financial wellbeing continuum and investigates how socio-demographic characteristics and multidimensional financial inclusion are associated with resilience outcomes in Saudi Arabia. item.title: Toward a hybrid digital twin of society: Quantifying cognitive–spatial linkages through online–offline feedback networks
item.description: Journal of Urban Mobility — Digital platforms increasingly shape how people experience and navigate cities, creating a link between virtual information seeking and physical mobility. Despite this growing interdependence, online and offline activities are often studied separately in urban mobility research. This paper proposes the concept and computational framework of the Feedback Network to capture the continuous interaction between cognitive activity in digital environments and behavior in physical space. item.title: A quantitative analysis of determinants and severity of rural poverty: a household level cross-sectional study in Rushinga rural district in Zimbabwe
item.description: Agrekon — Alleviating all forms of poverty is a priority for developing countries like Zimbabwe, but understanding the factors driving household-level rural poverty is vital for achieving the UN SDGs. This study compares the characteristics of poor and non-poor households, estimates ward-level poverty incidence, depth and severity, and examines the household- and location-level factors associated with consumption poverty in Rushinga Rural District, Zimbabwe. item.title: Perceptions and preferences of urban youth regarding informal green spaces
item.description: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering — The continued provision of formal urban green spaces (UGS) is constrained by land and management conditions, while informal green spaces (IGS) can supplement residents’ everyday contact with nature. Based on a field survey in Nankai District and 116 valid questionnaires from young adults in Tianjin, this study examined perceptions of and preferences for IGS and their relationships with sociodemographic characteristics, green-space participation, residential context, and general green-space attitudes. item.title: Measuring multidimensional housing pressure in equitable and resilient Australian cities
item.description: Discover Cities — Housing equity is central to resilient, inclusive and sustainable urban development. Yet housing policy is often framed narrowly around prices, rents, supply shortages or individual affordability stress. This paper develops the concept of common-good housing pressure to capture the spatial concentration of housing conditions that affect not only households, but also the wider functioning of cities. item.title: Three roles of evacuation simulation in life-safety-oriented flood disaster management
item.description: Journal of Coastal and Riverine Flood Risk — Evacuation simulation links physical hazard analysis with human response by assessing whether populations exposed to coastal and riverine flood hazards can reach safety within the available time. However, because evacuation is a collective process emerging from individual decisions made during infrequent and rapidly evolving events, behavioral realism, validation, and transferability remain challenging. item.title: Profiling privacy preservation against gradient inversion attacks in tabular federated learning
item.description: International Journal of Information Security — Federated learning (FL) enables multiple data holders to train machine learning models collaboratively without centralizing raw data, making it useful in privacy sensitive domains such as healthcare and institutional data sharing. FL keeps data local to clients while communicating only model updates, such as gradients or model deltas. Nevertheless, these updates can expose private client data through gradient inversion attacks (GIAs). item.description: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research — Now in its third year, Weather4cast 2023 again advanced modern algorithms in AI and machine learning through a highly topical interdisciplinary challenge at the NeurIPS Competition Track. Predicting hi-res rain radar movies from multi-band satellite sensors required data fusion of complementary signal sources and video frame prediction with super-resolution techniques. item.description: Nano Convergence — Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are among the most promising energy conversion technologies for achieving sustainable and carbon-neutral energy systems.
